spatial_claims.claim: E, F, G, H, K, L are midpoints of edges AB, AC, AD, BC, CD, BD respectively of tetrahedron ABCD
EF parallel to BC and EF = BC/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ABC)
EH parallel to AC and EH = AC/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ABC)
FH parallel to AB and FH = AB/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ABC)
EG parallel to BD and EG = BD/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ABD)
EL parallel to AD and EL = AD/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ABD)
GL parallel to AB and GL = AB/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ABD)
FG parallel to CD and FG = CD/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ACD)
FK parallel to AD and FK = AD/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ACD)
GK parallel to AC and GK = AC/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle ACD)
HK parallel to BD and HK = BD/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle BCD)
HL parallel to CD and HL = CD/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle BCD)
KL parallel to BC and KL = BC/2 (midpoint theorem in triangle BCD)
Pyramid AEFG has each edge half the corresponding edge of ABCD, so AEFG is similar to ABCD with ratio 1:2
Pyramid DGKL has each edge half the corresponding edge of ABCD, so DGKL is similar to ABCD with ratio 1:2
AEFG and DGKL have the same six edge lengths and are therefore congruent
EHKG is a parallelogram: opposite sides EH parallel to GK (both parallel to AC) and EG parallel to HK (both parallel to BD)
Plane of parallelogram EHKG divides the remaining solid into two parts, one containing F and C, the other containing L and B
EHCF is a parallelogram on face ABC (EF parallel to HC, EH parallel to CF)
FGKC is a parallelogram on face ACD (FG parallel to CK, GK parallel to CF)
Solid EFGHCK is a prism with congruent parallel triangular faces EFG and HCK
EBLG is a parallelogram on face ABD (EB parallel to GL, BL parallel to EG)
BHKL is a parallelogram on face BCD (BH parallel to KL, BL parallel to HK)
Solid EBHGKL is a prism with congruent parallel triangular faces EBH and GKL
Corner pyramid CFHK has same edge lengths as AEFG (all six edges are halves of ABCD edges)
Corner pyramid BEHL has same edge lengths as DGKL
Remainder of Prism 1 after removing CFHK is a pyramid on base EHKG with apex F
Remainder of Prism 2 after removing BEHL is a pyramid on base EHKG with apex L
F and L lie on opposite sides of plane EHKG and are equidistant from it
Prism 1 properly contains corner pyramid CFHK which equals AEFG, so Prism 1 > AEFG
Prism 2 properly contains corner pyramid BEHL which equals DGKL, so Prism 2 > DGKL
Two prisms together exceed the two removed pyramids, hence exceed half the whole

configuration_map: Tetrahedron ABCD with apex A and base BCD. Six midpoints: E on AB, F on AC, G on AD, H on BC, K on CD, L on BD. The three pairs of opposite edges are (AB,CD), (AC,BD), (AD,BC). Midpoints of edges AB,BC,CD,AD form parallelogram EHKG in a plane through the centroid (A+B+C+D)/4; its diagonals EK and HG bisect each other at the centroid. Midpoints F and L of the remaining opposite edge pair (AC,BD) lie on opposite sides of plane EHKG, equidistant from it (verified by coordinate computation: signed distances are -V/8 and +V/8 where V is the scalar triple product). Four corner sub-tetrahedra AEFG, BEHL, CFHK, DGKL are all congruent with edge lengths {AB/2, AC/2, AD/2, BC/2, BD/2, CD/2}. After removing AEFG (at A) and DGKL (at D), the central octahedron EFGHKL is split by plane EHKG into two pyramids with apex F and L. Prism 1 = CFHK + pyramid(EHKG,F) on the C-side. Prism 2 = BEHL + pyramid(EHKG,L) on the B-side. Volume accounting: each corner = V/8, each central pyramid = V/4, each prism = 3V/8, total 2(V/8) + 2(3V/8) = V. Two prisms = 3V/4 > V/2.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The midpoint parallelism claims follow correctly from VI.2 applied to each face. The parallelogram EHKG is verified by the diagonal midpoint coincidence (E+K = H+G). The prism identifications are correct with properly congruent and parallel triangular faces. The critical claim that F and L are equidistant from and on opposite sides of plane EHKG is verified by coordinate computation (signed distances are negatives of each other). The volume decomposition is complete and non-overlapping, with correct inequality for the final conclusion.
